name: Hautes-Côtes de Nuits

known.via: English Wikipedia "Hautes-Côtes de Nuits" (a wine place on Wikidata)

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards. The Grand Crus usually sit mid-slope and higher, with the best sun and drainage.

notes: Hautes Côtes de Nuits wines are sold as Bourgogne, with Hautes Côtes de Nuits added to the name.
About 22% of the wine is white, and the rest is red and rosé.
As Bourgogne wines, the reds often have fine, velvety tannins and lovely fruit.
The whites taste rich, lifted by the acidity they need for balance and aging.

blurb.text: A Burgundy sub-region on top of and behind the Côte de Nuits escarpment, in valleys and slopes. Its wines are labeled Bourgogne Hautes Côtes de Nuits, a named area within the Bourgogne AOC, for red wine based on Pinot Noir, white from Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc, and some rosé. It has no Premier Cru vineyards.
